cand.title: European Para Championships 2027
cand.excerpt: Strong event evidence; venue commitment reduces current access but supports targeted overflow/future capture.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Alexis Schäfer, EPC Head of Commercial, is explicitly named on the official partnerships page; the contact page publishes alexis@europeanparachampionships.com for partnerships. Eric Kersten is EPC founder and is identified as CEO in the 2027 programme announcement. These are verified commercial/senior routing contacts, not verified accommodation contract signatories. Claude Membrez, Palexpo General Director, and Henri della Casa, Canton of Geneva project manager, are additional verified venue/local coordination contacts; neither is established as a housing buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming second edition, 2–15 August 2027, within the requested horizon. These are activity dates, independently published by the event owner and Palexpo, not article dates. The 2 June 2026 programme announcement specifies 12 sports and more than 2,000 athletes expected. Do not interpret that as total attendance, room demand or confirmed registrations.
findings.hotelProductFit: Conditional inference: an airport-corridor lodging satellite is more plausible than hosting the championships or claiming a resort-retreat role. Using the supplied hotel brief, propose only a scoped 20–120-room enquiry within the 237-room property, not a forecast or whole-house claim; meetings/F&B could support briefings if requested. More than 2,000 expected athletes makes the event too large for a single-property solution. Founex is not a walkable Palexpo or city-centre base. YOTEL publishes Accessible Premium Queen rooms and accessible-compliant inventory, but no verified event-usable accessible-room count was established. Standard rooms are compact; athlete suitability requires a room-by-room and circulation audit. The hotel advertises an airport shuttle, not an EPC/Palexpo team shuttle. Accessible transport, equipment storage, dining and sport schedules must be agreed before offering athlete blocks. Officials, production/support staff or small delegations are potential segments, not evidenced bookings.
findings.venueCommitments: Palexpo Exhibition Halls 4–6 and Congress Centre, Route François-Peyrot 30, 1218 Le Grand-Saconnex, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland. Territory: Geneva Airport corridor, outside Geneva city municipality; not Founex/Nyon/La Côte or Lausanne. Geneva Tourism also names adjacent Parc Sarasin. EPC describes additional public locations across Geneva; a complete venue-by-sport allocation is not established. Public venue commitment is confirmed; the signed venue contract was not available. Palexpo is an exhibition/congress venue, not an incumbent hotel.
findings.historicalRotation: Inaugural edition: Rotterdam, Netherlands, 8–20 August 2023, centred on Rotterdam Ahoy with outdoor/city venues. Second edition: Geneva, 2–15 August 2027. Official recurrence is every four years, preceding the Paralympic Games; not annual and not a recurring Geneva hotel account. EPC is discussing 2031/2035 hosts, but the cited announcement identifies no selected city, venue or exact dates; these cycles are outside the research horizon.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Geneva 2027: unknown. No edition-specific housing bureau appointment, hotel contract, named hotel, published block, open RFP, allocation policy, peak-room figure or room-night total was located in the reviewed public evidence. No Geneva incumbent hotels can therefore be named. This does not establish that inventory is open or that no private contracts exist. Palexpo advertises a general housing service: “Whether you’re outlining your requirements or pre-booking a number of rooms…”; this is a possible referral channel, not evidence of EPC appointment. Historical precedent only: the Rotterdam 2023 guide says “All reservations during the registration procedure must be made through the Local Organizing Committee” and required official hotels for accreditation. Its nine hotels and published daily-room requirement are recorded under historicalEditions; none is a Geneva commitment.
findings.organizationStructure: European Para Championships BV owns the event concept and broadcast, sponsorship and marketing rights. This is a corporate rights-holder, not simply an association congress owned by an unnamed organizing body. The official hosting announcement describes a central EPC team plus national/local organizing structures. The Geneva collaboration update names Canton, venue and tourism stakeholders; it does not identify the Swiss contracting entity for accommodation or an appointed PCO/DMC. Palexpo is the venue, not the event owner. Do not conflate EPC BV with the European Paralympic Committee.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No sourced Geneva 2027 sell-out, shortage, overflow request, competing hotel award or exclusive housing contract was found. Do not sell this as verified overflow. Historical centralized booking and accessibility requirements are a warning about possible procurement restrictions, not proof of a 2027 restriction. Founex transfers and unverified accessible-room capacity are material disadvantages versus an on-site/near-venue solution. Palexpo venue confirmation limits venue displacement, not necessarily hotel access.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Alexis Schäfer via the published partnerships address, with Eric Kersten as senior escalation, asking for the named Geneva 2027 accommodation/procurement lead and Swiss contracting entity. Establish appointed housing channel, signed hotels/holds, remaining procurement timetable, accreditation booking rules and permission to offer Founex inventory. Request nightly demand by customer group, accessible-room specifications, transport standards and arrival/departure patterns. Only then present a capped 20–120-room option subject to hotel availability, accessibility audit and costed accessible Palexpo transfers; do not promise an existing airport shuttle can carry teams. Ask Palexpo for the accommodation lead if EPC refers the enquiry there; its generic housing service is not a confirmed appointment.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the next announced edition, Geneva 2027, event and venue are confirmed but hotel procurement accessibility remains unconfirmed. A supplier enquiry is justified; a sales-qualified open room block is not. No evidence establishes either that lodging is already committed elsewhere or that YOTEL can book accredited delegations independently.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: prioritize early qualification for Geneva 2027 rather than assuming a closed edition. If its housing is already allocated, ask about permitted supplementary staff/official lodging or documented overflow only. Preserve relationships for EPC planning visits or later programmes, but do not forecast local rooms from 2031/2035: hosts are not announced in the cited process update and rotation can move demand away from Geneva. Future host dialogue is not a hotel RFP.
